findings.detail: Kodansha directly says the painting in the school art room awakens Yatora’s interest; the supplied Tajimi, VIZ, and Yen Press passages support all three distractor notes. The prompt itself gives a strong everyday clue (painting); correctIndex 1 is exact. Broad adults can answer without knowing Blue Period. The note adds Yatora’s prior school situation from the same volume.

Yen Press directly supports the Sohmas turning into Chinese Zodiac animals. NASA passages support the seasonal cycle, lunar month and Western signs used in the distractors. The animal-per-sign clue and familiar twelve-animal system make the answer broadly accessible; correctIndex 2 is exact.

The saved GKIDS passage explicitly says Chihiro must find a way to free her parents. Saved VIZ passages support the Fullmetal, Demon Slayer and One Piece distractor notes. The MAIN asks the family-rescue fact, distinct from prior Spirited Away title, award and director relations at this ID, #71 and world-cinema #26. This is a central plot fact of a widely known film; no exhausted prior source claim was reopened and no third attempt was made.

Studio Ghibli lists Diana Wynne Jones as the original-work author, and the saved Folio Society passage identifies Howl’s Moving Castle as Jones’s 1986 book; supplied Slam Dunk, JFDB and Gundam contexts support the three distractor notes. CorrectIndex 3 is exact and the answer note adds the screenplay/director fact. The prompt requires knowing that a relatively unfamiliar author’s source work is a novel; knowing the film or author name alone does not make that fact broadly known to adults. Preserve frozen easy rating as HOLD.

Kodansha explicitly identifies Inori as dreaming of becoming a figure skater and describes her rink training; saved Crunchyroll, World Curling and ISU passages support the notes. The peer check found a close hit at winter-sports #3 (and #59): both generalize figure-skating characteristics, while this MAIN is the story-specific Inori-to-sport relation. It is adjacent but not the same MAIN or its inverse. Prompt clues make the easy answer accessible; correctIndex 1 is exact.

GKIDS directly states that near-sighted Jiro cannot be a pilot and becomes an airplane designer inspired by Caproni. National Film Archive, Kodansha and Crunchyroll saved passages support all distractor notes. The prompt clue and options make the answer broadly accessible; correctIndex 2 is exact.

Natsume’s full saved passage describes the Thai Bats & Terry edition flipped from the Japanese original: the right-handed pitcher becomes left-handed and screen-tone lettering reverses. The operation and all three alternatives are correctly distinguished. The requested card-games #93 comparator is the Pokémon TCG prize-card win condition and has no shared MAIN/inverse relation. The explicit reversed lettering/handedness clue makes the operation accessible; correctIndex 3 is exact.

Netflix Tudum explicitly distinguishes Cosmos as jazz and Spokey Dokey as blues in Cowboy Bebop; Smithsonian supports bebop as a jazz style, and Yen Press supports the Bocchi distractor. CorrectIndex 1 and note facts are exact. However, identifying bebop as a jazz subgenre is specialist music knowledge for a broad adult audience; the second anime-specific clue does not make this easy without familiarity with the show or jazz. Preserve frozen easy rating as HOLD.

Kodansha directly says Thorfinn was raised by Vikings, and names Leif Ericson and Vinland. Library of Congress and Royal Museums Greenwich passages support the Marco Polo, buccaneer and San Gabriel notes. CorrectIndex 1 is exact; Leif/Vinland are widely recognizable historical clues for a broad audience.

Yen Press directly describes Lucius as a Roman architect working on thermae and a new bathhouse. The Colosseum, UNESCO Pont du Gard and Italian museum passages support the three distractor notes. The translated title/context supply a plain-language clue; correctIndex 2 is exact.
